title: DEFINED: A Data-Efficient Computational Framework for Fine-Grained Creativity Assessment in Debate Scenarios

problem.claim: Assessing creativity in complex, open-ended environments such as debate is difficult.

gap.claim: Existing approaches rely on standardized simple tasks, scarce fine-grained expert data, costly human evaluation, and methods poorly suited to complex settings.

contributions.claim: A data-efficient framework for fine-grained creativity assessment in debate scenarios.
A hierarchical eight-dimensional creativity metric system supporting fine-grained and coarse-grained evaluation through a hierarchical scoring head.
A constrained data augmentation and mixed-granularity training strategy for learning from authentic debate data and limited fine-grained supervision.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The evaluation reports that the scoring model achieves accurate and stable scoring.
The scoring model is reported to outperform prompt-based large language model evaluators and existing debate scoring methods.
An empirical study with debate-naive participants is used as a qualitative case study for mid-to-low proficiency populations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Creativity is important, but assessing it in complex open-ended environments is challenging.
Debate is presented as an ecologically valid, multidimensional, and data-rich assessment context.
Current automated scoring methods are poorly suited to debate and still depend on costly human evaluation.
DEFINED combines hierarchical creativity metrics, a pretrained autoregressive model, authentic debate data, augmentation, and mixed-granularity training.
The authors evaluate ecological validity with debate-naive participants and report accurate, stable, and comparatively stronger scoring.

unknowns: The eight metric dimensions are not defined.
Dataset size, splits, annotation protocol, and score distributions are omitted.
Quantitative evaluation results and baseline details are omitted.
The effects of augmentation and mixed-granularity training are not isolated.
